items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1978-Fall Transcript
items.q: And he wanted to learn to play the piano. And I wanted to really learn to sing, because I wasn't singing too much there, you know? So, a lot of jazz. And this is how I and him got together.

ctx.x: Uh, did you play kind of in a touring group with, going from club to club with Jack Dupree and, uh, somebody told me Red Fox too.

Well, Red Fox didn't play music. Right. He was just a comedian at that time. And we all stuck together back in the 30s, 33, 37, 38, things started to picking up. Uh, this is when I met Jack Dupree around 1937, 38. And he was a comedian also. He sung the blues and he wore union suits out on the stage. Well, at that time I was a one man's band, you know? I did everything. He said, I beat my own drum. I did my own whistling and singing and harmonizing. And I played my own melody. And he wanted to learn to play the…

items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1975-11-13
items.q: We had Jack Dupreak with us then, because Jack Dupreak was singing in the community then. He wasn't playing music. I learned him a little bit about the piano and he learned me a little bit about the blues and singing lines.

ctx.x: So what was the first time you tried to form a group? Was there a point where you tried to form a group? You know, first really get out and perform in front of people.

In front of people? Well, I got a chance to do that with, uh, well, we was working at the Cotton Club. We had a mixed group then. Let me see who was with us. We had Jack Dupreak with us then, because Jack Dupreak was singing in the community then. He wasn't playing music. I learned him a little bit about the piano and he learned me a little bit about the blues and singing lines. So we just transferred one thing to the other.
